original_question: Let D be a finite distributive lattice that is the glued sum D^h u B2 of a finite distributive lattice D^h with B2, and let L be a patch lattice, meaning a rectangular lattice whose corners are dual atoms; equivalently, patch lattices are exactly those rectangular lattices L for which Con L is a glued sum of a finite distributive lattice Con^h L with B2. Which properties of the finite distributive lattice Con^h L characterize exactly when D is the congruence lattice of a patch lattice L?
target_in_paper: Section 11, "Patch Problem" (the related open problem at the end of the survey, not the main SPS-lattice characterization problem from Section 5). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it uses the same decomposition of a finite distributive lattice D as a glued sum with B2, the same description of a patch lattice as a rectangular lattice whose corners are dual atoms, and the same reformulation that patch lattices are exactly those rectangular lattices whose congruence lattice is a glued sum of some finite distributive lattice with B2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))
missing_details: The paper states this as the labeled "Patch Problem" in Section 11, which is a related end-of-paper problem distinct from the main Section 5 problem about SPS lattices. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))

The quantifier structure should be existential: given D (equivalently given D^h), determine whether there exists a finite patch lattice L with Con L isomorphic to D. The draft's opening "let L be a patch lattice" is slightly circular for an existence/representation problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))

To be fully stand-alone, B2 should be identified as the four-element Boolean lattice, and the glued sum should be explained as gluing the top of D^h to the bottom of B2. The paper uses this notation in Section 11 without rederiving it there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))

To be paper-faithful, "rectangular lattice" should inherit the ambient meaning from Section 7.2: a finite planar semimodular lattice whose left and right boundary chains have unique doubly irreducible elements that are complementary. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))

The characterization in the paper is phrased in terms of the abstract finite distributive lattice D^h, not in terms of an already chosen lattice-specific object Con^h L. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))

The conclusion should be stated up to isomorphism: D is the congruence lattice of a patch lattice means D isomorphic to Con L for some finite patch lattice L. This matches the paper's representation language. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier such as "for all sufficiently large m" is relevant here; those issue-types are not part of this lattice-theoretic problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))
refined_question: Let B2 be the four-element Boolean lattice, and let D be a finite distributive lattice obtained as the glued sum of a finite distributive lattice D^h and B2, i.e. by identifying the top element of D^h with the bottom element of B2. A finite planar semimodular lattice L is called rectangular if its left and right boundary chains have unique doubly irreducible elements that are complementary, and L is a patch lattice if, in addition, its corners are dual atoms. Since the paper notes that a rectangular lattice is a patch lattice exactly when its congruence lattice has the form E glued-sum B2 for some finite distributive lattice E, what necessary and sufficient properties of D^h characterize exactly when there exists a finite patch lattice L such that Con L isomorphic to D? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, characterize precisely which finite distributive lattices D of the form D = D^h glued-sum B2 occur as congruence lattices of finite patch lattices. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's final labeled open problem, not the earlier SPS-lattice problem. In Section 11 the author first fixes a finite distributive lattice D of the form D^h glued-sum B2, then recalls the equivalence that a rectangular lattice is a patch lattice iff its congruence lattice is of that same glued-sum form, and then asks for a characterization in terms of the finite distributive lattice D^h. That is exactly what the refined question preserves, while removing the slight circularity of introducing a patch lattice L before asking whether D can be represented as Con L. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))
